files.README.md:
# Atlas

Atlas runs a whole simulated machine - processes, filesystem, network, browser -
from a seed, and replays it byte for byte.

Same seed, same inputs, same bytes out.

## Quick start

```
cargo add atlas
cargo run --example company -- --seed 42 --ticks 1200
```

The example boots the `company` world, runs it for 1200 ticks and prints the
digest of everything the machines drew. Run it twice; the digests match.

## What is deterministic

- Time: every service is handed a tick, never a wall clock.
- Randomness: one stream per service, seeded from `service/{id}/initialize`.
- Order: anything unordered is a bug waiting for a Windows runner to find it.

## Links

- Handbook: http://intranet.internal/
- Walkthrough: http://youtube.com/watch?v=atlas-walkthrough
- Status: http://status.northstar.example/
- Product: http://northstar.example/product

## License

MIT, see `LICENSE`.

files.docs/determinism.md:
# Why the same seed gives the same bytes

Atlas never asks the host what time it is, never reads `/dev/urandom` and never
iterates a structure whose order the language does not promise.

## Time

Every service is handed a tick. A tick is an integer.

## Randomness

One stream per service, seeded from `service/{id}/initialize`, so adding a service
never changes another's draws.

## Order

TODO: the BFS story from #14.

9.title: Document the seeded determinism streams
9.body: Every service draws from service/{id}/initialize, so insertion order does not perturb anyone else. That is worth a paragraph in CONTRIBUTING.md.
9.author: praman

comments.author: cnakamura
comments.body: Taking this with the contributing guide, #11.

12.title: Expose the tick clock through the CLI
12.body: `atlas run` should accept `--ticks N` and print the final tick, so a replay script can assert on it without parsing the digest.
12.author: bmartinez

comments.author: alicechen
comments.body: Agreed. The clock module already has everything the flag needs.

13.title: Typo in CONTRIBUTING.md: rule 3 says 'directory listing' twice
13.body: Small one, good for a first PR.
13.author: cnakamura

14.title: BFS path test fails on Windows only
14.body:
tests/path.rs is green on Linux and macOS and red on the Windows runner about one run in four.

Repro: http://github.com/gist/flaky-repro

The fixture has two equal-length paths from alice-mac to app-server and the test assumes the same one comes back every time.
14.author: bmartinez

comments.author: alicechen
comments.body: Smells like hash-map iteration order - src/bfs.rs walks links.get(at) straight out of a HashMap.

comments.author: praman
comments.body: It is. I wrote the long version here: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/t-4411

16.title: Release build warns about an unused import in src/seed.rs
16.body: `cargo build --release` prints one warning. Zero warnings is the rule.
16.author: alicechen

17.title: Replay diverges when the seed is zero
17.body: With `--seed 0` two runs disagree after tick 800. Every other seed I tried is stable. Suspect the per-service stream collapses to the same value for every service.
17.author: praman

comments.author: alicechen
comments.body: stream() xors the seed into a constant; with 0 that constant is shared by every service. Nice catch.

18.title: Publish a determinism explainer for the launch
18.body: The launch checklist wants one page a reader can send to a sceptic. Draft lives in the launch doc: http://docs.google.com/documents/atlas-launch
18.author: cnakamura

20.title: Does Atlas run on Windows ARM?
20.body: The CI matrix only lists x64 runners. Is ARM supported or just untested?
20.author: dvasquez

15.title: Sort refs before iterating in BFS
15.body:
Swap the HashMap for a BTreeMap so neighbour order is part of the contract, and pin that order in the test.

Closes #14.
15.author: praman
15.head: refs/heads/sort-refs

comments.author: bmartinez
comments.body: Ran it 200 times on the Windows matrix. Green every time.

reviews.author: bmartinez
reviews.body: The test still builds a HashMap fixture on line 4; it should use the same map type as the router.

reviews.author: alicechen
reviews.body: Exactly right. The map was never the fast path anyway.

19.title: Draft the determinism explainer
19.body: First pass at the page #18 asks for. The Order section is still a TODO until #15 lands.
19.author: cnakamura
19.head: refs/heads/determinism-doc
